questions.q: Where do you usually go shopping?
questions.answer: For everyday things, I go to the local market near our home, which is always [[bustling]]. For larger purchases, I'd rather order online or visit one of the bigger shopping centres, where there's more choice.
It depends what I'm shopping for, honestly. I like buying books or a bit of tech, but clothes shopping [[drains]] me quickly. These days I do most of it online, which saves me a lot of time.

questions.q: Do you prefer shopping alone or with others?
questions.answer: Alone, usually, because I like to get in and out quickly. When I go with my sister, it turns into an afternoon of [[browsing]] every single shop, which is fun occasionally but exhausting.

questions.q: Do you ever buy things on impulse?
questions.answer: Occasionally, especially books. If I see an interesting title, I find it hard to resist, even if I already have a pile waiting to be read. Otherwise, I'm fairly [[prudent]] with what I spend.

questions.q: Has the way people shop in your country changed?
questions.answer: Dramatically. Not long ago almost everyone shopped at markets, but now online shopping and home delivery are extremely common, especially in cities. Still, traditional markets remain [[resilient]], because people enjoy bargaining and seeing products in person.
